name: analytics-cjs-build
goal: Keep analytics persistence available to Bun while its desktop CommonJS bundle passes the existing Node syntax check.

steps.title: Identify the failing behavior, expected behavior, and reproduction.
steps.evidence: At e812 on harbor-mbp-2 the existing game build case fails because the desktop CommonJS bundle contains import.meta from AnalyticsRepository; Node syntax validation rejects it.

steps.title: Explain why existing standardized tests missed the bug; name the scenario, fixture, lifecycle or assertion gap and reusable test change.
steps.evidence: The existing case catches the syntax failure but does not prove a cold Node import of the bundled analytics boundary or real Bun SQLite persistence. Extend that same build case with both checks.

steps.title: Strengthen the existing standardized test; commit it before repair, run it failing with loop record --phase red, and preserve the assertion.
steps.evidence: Clean snapshot 27ff791f failed the unchanged game build case with Node 24 rejecting import.meta in main.cjs; red record 7771f3fa8a0c4628f5e54f48d5f2857dac5a605bd82bbf6fb9d19bfa4a56bb83.

steps.title: Implement the smallest repair without weakening the regression test.
steps.evidence: Use an executable-based require base for Bun builtins and translate only the sandbox resolver in desktop CommonJS builds. Native source and packaged synthetic sandbox checks passed; real providers remain unqualified.

steps.title: Rerun the same unchanged regression test at a separate fix commit with loop record --phase green; preserve passing proof.
steps.evidence: The same clean-snapshot test passed at 32e0552b under the identical guarded environment; red record 0cd22d9358f20d061de36b7cb11842ef1330a6c75394e70baa44446dba5b1765 and green record a75ae2ccb92a8302183f93b62256f8f0ee8184b3fb08177bf3748ce9001bad87.

steps.title: Run relevant project checks and affected UI browser flows with fresh inspected screenshots and no unexpected browser errors; preserve diagnostics and keep pending until proof passes.
Prove both original loader failures remain detectable.
